question.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
question.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $v\times a,||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨1,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\times ⟨0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & \operatorname{cos}⁡t & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 0 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t & -\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡t & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡t & -\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}1 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 0 & -\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}1 & \operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 0 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨(-{cos}^{2}⁡t-{sin}^{2}⁡t),-(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\operatorname{cos}⁡t,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{2} \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
